label: Close
description: End the exchange with this run's caller, saying why: a close frame (`code`, `reason`) behind a Socket, a response (`status`, `reason` as the String body) behind a Route. It needs no data from upstream, so `_should_flow` is usually its whole wiring: prefill `reason` and `status` and gate it on the branch that should end here (a Switch's failing case, say).

inputs.name: code
inputs.label: Close code (Socket, empty = 1000)
inputs.description: WebSocket close code, Socket only: empty is 1000, 4000 to 4999 are yours.

inputs.name: reason
inputs.description: Short sentence for the caller: the close frame's reason, or the response body. Refused after a Stream.

inputs.name: status
inputs.label: Status (Route, empty = 204, or 200 with a reason)
inputs.description: HTTP status, Route only: empty is 204 without a reason, 200 with one; 204 with a reason is refused. Ignored after a Stream (the status already went out).

inputs.name: headers
inputs.label: Headers (Route)
inputs.description: Extra response headers, Route only (a 304's `etag`, a 429's `retry-after`); a content-type overrides the reason's. Refused after a Stream.

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: True once the exchange has ended.

then.message: Close '{id}' answers nobody: no trigger with a live caller (a Route, a Socket) starts a run that reaches it. Wire it from the trigger's run (through data, or `_should_flow`), or put it in a group the trigger's `_should_flow` runs.
Close '{id}' has a `reason` and `status: 204`: a 204 carries no body, so the message would never reach the caller. Pick a status that carries one (400, 403, 404, 409...), or drop `reason`.
Close '{id}' sets `code`, the WebSocket close code, but an HTTP caller (a Route) starts the run that reaches it. Say how it ended with `status` (and `reason`) instead.
Close '{id}' sets `status`, an HTTP status, but a WebSocket caller (a Socket) starts the run that reaches it. A close frame carries `code` and `reason` instead.
